title: Past Simple: regulares e irregulares
instructions: Completá con el Past Simple (afirmativo, negativo o pregunta) del verbo entre paréntesis.
text:
1. She [1] (forget) to submit the report yesterday.
2. We [2] (go) to the conference last week.
3. I [3] (not / see) the error message.
4. [4] (you / find) the bug yesterday?
5. He [5] (buy) a new laptop two days ago.
6. The server [6] (crash) and then it [7] (restart).
7. She [8] (teach) me how to use Git.
8. They [9] (not / be) at the meeting.

pat: forget es irregular: forget → forgot → forgotten. Pasado simple: forgot.
items.e: forget es irregular: forget → forgot → forgotten.

pat: go es irregular: go → went → gone. Pasado simple: went.
items.e: go → went (Past Simple); 'gone' es el participio.

pat: después de didn't el verbo va en forma base: didn't see.
el negativo del pasado simple se arma con didn't + verbo base.
items.e: Negativo: didn't + verbo BASE aunque sea irregular (Unit2/02).

pat: después de did el verbo va en forma base: did you find.
la pregunta en pasado simple se arma con did + sujeto + verbo base: did you find.
items.e: Pregunta: Did + sujeto + verbo base.

pat: buy es irregular: buy → bought → bought.
items.e: buy → bought → bought.
Verbo regular: + -ed.
'and then' → dos acciones en secuencia, ambas Past Simple.

pat: teach es irregular: teach → taught → taught.
items.e: teach → taught → taught.

pat: they → weren't (was/were: they, we, you → were).
el verbo be no usa did/didn't; su negativo es wasn't/weren't.
items.e: they → were; el verbo to be no usa did.

title: Past Simple o Past Continuous (when / while)
instructions: Completá con la forma correcta del verbo entre paréntesis.
text:
1. While I [1] (reboot) the server, the client suddenly disconnected.
2. She [2] (talk) on the phone when the power went out.
3. What [3] (you / do) when the bug appeared?
4. When I [4] (open) the door, my husband was painting the kitchen.
5. I [5] (walk) to work when it started to rain.
6. They [6] (work) on the project all morning, so they missed the call.
7. He [7] (not / know) the answer.
8. While Ana [8] (write) code, Luis [9] (test) it.

pat: while marca una acción en progreso que fue interrumpida: was rebooting.
items.e: Acción larga en progreso + interrupción (disconnected) → Past Continuous.

pat: la acción estaba en progreso cuando algo la interrumpió (power went out): was talking.
she → was (was: I, he, she, it).
items.e: Acción de fondo interrumpida por 'the power went out'.

pat: en la pregunta el auxiliar va antes del sujeto: were you doing.
when the bug appeared interrumpe una acción en progreso: were you doing.
items.e: Pregunta: were + sujeto + -ing (el auxiliar va ANTES del sujeto).

pat: la acción corta (abrir la puerta) es la que ocurrió en un momento: opened. La que estaba en progreso es painting.
items.e: La interrupción/momento puntual → Past Simple; 'was painting' es la acción de fondo.

pat: caminaba cuando empezó a llover (acción en progreso interrumpida): was walking.
items.e: Acción en progreso interrumpida por 'it started to rain'.

pat: all morning marca duración (acción en progreso): were working.
items.e: 'all morning' → acción prolongada en progreso → Past Continuous.

pat: know es un state verb y no se usa en forma continua: didn't know.
items.e: know = state verb → no va en continuo.

pat: while marca dos acciones simultáneas en progreso: was writing.
items.e: 'while' → acciones en paralelo → ambas Past Continuous.

pat: while marca dos acciones simultáneas en progreso: was testing.
items.e: Segunda acción en paralelo.

title: Past Perfect: ¿qué ocurrió antes?
instructions: Completá con la forma correcta (Past Perfect o Past Simple según el contexto).
text:
1. By the time she arrived, the developer [1] (fix) all the bugs.
2. The app crashed after he [2] (update) it.
3. She [3] (not / read) the documentation before you asked.
4. The server crashed because someone [4] (delete) the wrong file.
5. When I [5] (look) everywhere for my keys, I started to panic.
6. [6] (they / finish) the tests before the release?
7. He [7] (never / use) Docker before he joined the company.
8. We [8] (eat) before you arrived.
9. She [9] (go) home before the meeting started.

pat: by the time marca que lo arreglado ocurrió ANTES de que ella llegara: had fixed.
la historia está en pasado: had fixed (had + participio), no have.
items.e: 'By the time' → algo ya estaba hecho antes → Past Perfect.
Primero actualizó, después se cayó: la acción anterior va en Past Perfect.
items.altnote: Correcta con aviso: con after el orden de los hechos ya está claro, así que el pasado simple es natural. El ejercicio pide marcar la acción anterior con past perfect (had updated); en el examen, si la consigna pide 'lo que pasó antes', elegí had + participio.

pat: el participio de read se escribe read (read → read → read): hadn't read.
items.e: Negativo: hadn't + participio (read se escribe igual).
items.altnote: Correcta con aviso: con before el orden de los hechos ya está claro, así que el pasado simple es natural. El ejercicio pide marcar la acción anterior con past perfect (hadn't read); en el examen, si la consigna pide 'lo que pasó antes', elegí had + participio.

items.e: 'because someone had deleted': la causa ocurrió antes del crash.
items.altnote: Correcta con aviso: con because el orden de los hechos ya está claro, así que el pasado simple es natural. El ejercicio pide marcar la acción anterior con past perfect (had deleted); en el examen, si la consigna pide 'lo que pasó antes', elegí had + participio.

pat: buscó en todos lados ANTES de entrar en pánico. Past perfect marca la acción anterior: had looked.
was looking sería una acción en progreso al mismo tiempo; acá buscar terminó antes del pánico: had looked.
items.e: Ejemplo de tu apunte: primero buscó, después entró en pánico.

pat: en la pregunta el auxiliar va antes del sujeto: had they finished.
items.e: Pregunta: Had + sujeto + participio.
items.altnote: Correcta con aviso: con before el orden de los hechos ya está claro, así que el pasado simple es natural. El ejercicio pide marcar la acción anterior con past perfect (had they finished); en el examen, si la consigna pide 'lo que pasó antes', elegí had + participio.

pat: el adverbio va entre had y el participio: had never used.
items.e: 'never ... before' → Past Perfect; el adverbio va entre had y el participio.
items.altnote: Correcta con aviso: con before el orden de los hechos ya está claro, así que el pasado simple es natural. El ejercicio pide marcar la acción anterior con past perfect (had never used); en el examen, si la consigna pide 'lo que pasó antes', elegí had + participio.

pat: el participio de eat es eaten (eat → ate → eaten).
items.e: eat → ate → eaten (participio).
items.altnote: Correcta con aviso: con before el orden de los hechos ya está claro, así que el pasado simple es natural. El ejercicio pide marcar la acción anterior con past perfect (had eaten); en el examen, si la consigna pide 'lo que pasó antes', elegí had + participio.

pat: el participio de go es gone (go → went → gone).
items.e: go → went → gone. Con had va el participio.
items.altnote: Correcta con aviso: con before el orden de los hechos ya está claro, así que el pasado simple es natural. El ejercicio pide marcar la acción anterior con past perfect (had gone); en el examen, si la consigna pide 'lo que pasó antes', elegí had + participio.

title: Past Perfect Continuous: duración antes de otro evento
instructions: Completá con la forma correcta del verbo entre paréntesis.
text:
1. They [1] (look) for hours before they found the missing semicolon.
2. How long [2] (you / write) code before you realized it was the wrong branch?
3. He was exhausted! He [3] (code) for 36 hours.
4. The team [4] (refactor) the code for weeks when the project was cancelled.
5. She [5] (know) him for years before they worked together.
6. Her clothes were covered in paint. She [6] (paint) the ceiling for hours. (foco en el proceso)

pat: for hours marca una duración ANTES de encontrar el error: had been looking.
items.e: 'for hours' + antes de otro evento pasado → had been + -ing.

pat: how long ... before marca duración anterior a otro evento: had you been writing.
en la pregunta el auxiliar va antes del sujeto: had you been writing.
items.e: 'How long ... before' → duración: Had + sujeto + been + -ing.

pat: for 36 hours marca duración que llegó hasta ese momento del pasado: had been coding.
items.e: 'for 36 hours' antes de 'was exhausted'.

pat: for weeks marca duración anterior a otro evento (the project was cancelled): had been refactoring.
items.e: Duración antes de un corte en el pasado (Unit2/01).

pat: know es un state verb y no se usa en forma continua: had known.
la relación empezó antes de trabajar juntos (for years before): had known.
items.e: know = state verb → Past Perfect Simple, no Continuous.

pat: el foco está en el proceso y su duración, que dejó una consecuencia visible: had been painting.
items.e: El foco está en el proceso ('for hours') → had been painting.

title: Auxiliares del pasado: did / was / were / had
instructions: Escribí la pregunta o negación correcta. Cada tiempo tiene su propio auxiliar.
text:
1. [1] (she / go) to the meeting?
2. I [2] (not / work) late yesterday.
3. [3] (they / be) at home?
4. He [4] (not / go) to the meeting yesterday.
5. [5] (she / work) on the feature when the client called?
6. Where [6] (they / go) after the meeting?
7. I [7] (be) tired yesterday.
8. [8] (he / already / leave) when you arrived?

pat: después de did el verbo va en forma base: did she go.
después de did el verbo va en forma base, sin -s: did she go.
es una acción terminada en el pasado (pasado simple): did she go.
items.e: Did + sujeto + verbo base (Did she go? ✔ / Did she went? ✘).

pat: después de didn't el verbo va en forma base: didn't work.
el negativo del pasado simple se arma con didn't + verbo base.
items.e: didn't + verbo base.

pat: el verbo be no usa did; la pregunta invierte el verbo: were they.
items.e: they → were; en pregunta va antes del sujeto.

pat: después de didn't el verbo va en forma base: didn't go.
yesterday sin otro evento anterior pide pasado simple: didn't go.
items.e: 'yesterday' + una sola acción → Past Simple negativo.

pat: when the client called interrumpe una acción en progreso: was she working.
en la pregunta el auxiliar va antes del sujeto: was she working.
items.e: Acción en progreso interrumpida por 'the client called'.

pat: después de did el verbo va en forma base: did they go.
en la pregunta el auxiliar va antes del sujeto: did they go.
items.e: Pregunta con Where + did + sujeto + verbo base.

pat: el verbo be no usa did: I was.
items.e: I → was.

pat: la salida ocurrió ANTES de que llegaras: had he already left.
^had he already leaved$|^had he already went$
el participio de leave es left (leave → left → left).
items.e: 'when you arrived' → ya se había ido antes: Had + sujeto + participio.

title: ¿Qué tiempo del pasado es?
instructions: Elegí el tiempo verbal de la parte en negrita. Traducí al español para confirmar.

items.e: 'yesterday' → acción terminada (trabajé).

Past Continuous: Past Continuous = was/were + -ing: acción en progreso en el pasado. Acá tenés worked (verbo en pasado).
Past Perfect Simple: Past Perfect Simple = had + participio: ocurrió ANTES de otro momento del pasado. Acá tenés worked (verbo en pasado).
Past Perfect Continuous: Past Perfect Continuous = had been + -ing: duración ANTES de otro momento del pasado. Acá tenés worked (verbo en pasado).
used to (hábito pasado): used to = hábito o estado del pasado que ya no existe. Acá tenés worked (verbo en pasado).

items.q: She **was looking** at the screen when the error appeared.
items.e: estaba mirando + interrupción.

Past Simple: Past Simple = acción terminada en un momento del pasado (worked, took). Acá tenés was looking (was + -ing).
Past Perfect Simple: Past Perfect Simple = had + participio: ocurrió ANTES de otro momento del pasado. Acá tenés was looking (was + -ing).
Past Perfect Continuous: Past Perfect Continuous = had been + -ing: duración ANTES de otro momento del pasado. Acá tenés was looking (was + -ing).
used to (hábito pasado): used to = hábito o estado del pasado que ya no existe. Acá tenés was looking (was + -ing).

items.q: She **had looked** at the logs before calling me.
items.e: había mirado, antes de otro evento.

Past Simple: Past Simple = acción terminada en un momento del pasado (worked, took). Acá tenés had looked (had + participio).
Past Continuous: Past Continuous = was/were + -ing: acción en progreso en el pasado. Acá tenés had looked (had + participio).
Past Perfect Continuous: Past Perfect Continuous = had been + -ing: duración ANTES de otro momento del pasado. Acá tenés had looked (had + participio).
used to (hábito pasado): used to = hábito o estado del pasado que ya no existe. Acá tenés had looked (had + participio).

items.q: She **had been looking** at the logs for an hour when she found the bug.
items.e: había estado mirando + for an hour.

Past Simple: Past Simple = acción terminada en un momento del pasado (worked, took). Acá tenés had been looking (had been + -ing).
Past Continuous: Past Continuous = was/were + -ing: acción en progreso en el pasado. Acá tenés had been looking (had been + -ing).
Past Perfect Simple: Past Perfect Simple = had + participio: ocurrió ANTES de otro momento del pasado. Acá tenés had been looking (had been + -ing).
used to (hábito pasado): used to = hábito o estado del pasado que ya no existe. Acá tenés had been looking (had been + -ing).

items.e: tomó: acción puntual.

Past Continuous: Past Continuous = was/were + -ing: acción en progreso en el pasado. Acá tenés took (pasado irregular).
Past Perfect Simple: Past Perfect Simple = had + participio: ocurrió ANTES de otro momento del pasado. Acá tenés took (pasado irregular).
Past Perfect Continuous: Past Perfect Continuous = had been + -ing: duración ANTES de otro momento del pasado. Acá tenés took (pasado irregular).
used to (hábito pasado): used to = hábito o estado del pasado que ya no existe. Acá tenés took (pasado irregular).

items.q: He **had taken** the wrong file before anyone noticed.
items.e: había tomado, antes de que alguien lo notara.

Past Simple: Past Simple = acción terminada en un momento del pasado (worked, took). Acá tenés had taken (had + participio).
Past Continuous: Past Continuous = was/were + -ing: acción en progreso en el pasado. Acá tenés had taken (had + participio).
Past Perfect Continuous: Past Perfect Continuous = had been + -ing: duración ANTES de otro momento del pasado. Acá tenés had taken (had + participio).
used to (hábito pasado): used to = hábito o estado del pasado que ya no existe. Acá tenés had taken (had + participio).

items.e: no estaba siendo procesada: proceso en curso (Continuous pasivo).

Past Simple: Past Simple = acción terminada en un momento del pasado (worked, took). Acá tenés was not being processed (was + being + participio: pasivo continuo).
Past Perfect Simple: Past Perfect Simple = had + participio: ocurrió ANTES de otro momento del pasado. Acá tenés was not being processed (was + being + participio: pasivo continuo).
Past Perfect Continuous: Past Perfect Continuous = had been + -ing: duración ANTES de otro momento del pasado. Acá tenés was not being processed (was + being + participio: pasivo continuo).
used to (hábito pasado): used to = hábito o estado del pasado que ya no existe. Acá tenés was not being processed (was + being + participio: pasivo continuo).

items.e: Antes desplegábamos a mano (ya no).

Past Simple: Past Simple = acción terminada en un momento del pasado (worked, took). Acá tenés used to + verbo.
Past Continuous: Past Continuous = was/were + -ing: acción en progreso en el pasado. Acá tenés used to + verbo.
Past Perfect Simple: Past Perfect Simple = had + participio: ocurrió ANTES de otro momento del pasado. Acá tenés used to + verbo.
Past Perfect Continuous: Past Perfect Continuous = had been + -ing: duración ANTES de otro momento del pasado. Acá tenés used to + verbo.

items.q: They **had been working** on that feature for weeks when the project was cancelled.
items.e: for weeks, antes de la cancelación.

Past Simple: Past Simple = acción terminada en un momento del pasado (worked, took). Acá tenés had been working (had been + -ing).
Past Continuous: Past Continuous = was/were + -ing: acción en progreso en el pasado. Acá tenés had been working (had been + -ing).
Past Perfect Simple: Past Perfect Simple = had + participio: ocurrió ANTES de otro momento del pasado. Acá tenés had been working (had been + -ing).
used to (hábito pasado): used to = hábito o estado del pasado que ya no existe. Acá tenés had been working (had been + -ing).

items.q: The programmer ___ to submit the report yesterday.
items.e: 'yesterday' → Past Simple: forgot.

forget: yesterday pide pasado simple; forget es irregular (forget → forgot → forgotten): forgot.
has forgotten: yesterday es un momento CERRADO: pasado simple (forgot), no Present Perfect.
was forgetting: olvidarse fue un hecho puntual terminado, no una acción en progreso: forgot.

items.q: While I ___ the server, the client disconnected.
items.e: While + acción en progreso.

rebooted: while marca una acción en progreso que fue interrumpida: was rebooting.
had rebooted: had rebooted = ya había reiniciado ANTES. Con while la acción es simultánea y estaba en progreso: was rebooting.

items.q: By the time I got there, she ___ the whole flat by herself.
items.e: 'By the time' → ya estaba hecho antes de llegar.

painted: by the time marca que pintar ocurrió ANTES de que llegara, y ya estaba terminado: had painted.
was painting: was painting sería una acción en progreso; whole flat indica que ya estaba terminado cuando llegué: had painted.
has painted: Present Perfect habla del presente; la frase está en pasado (got there): had painted.

items.q: We ___ for two hours when the power went out.
items.e: for two hours + corte en el pasado.

were work: were + -ing (were working); aun así, for two hours marca duración anterior: had been working.
worked: for two hours marca una duración que llegó hasta un momento del pasado (when the power went out): had been working.
have been working: have been working es Present Perfect Continuous; la historia está en pasado: had been working.

items.e: Did + verbo base.

deleted: después de did el verbo va en forma base: Did she delete.
deleting: después de did el verbo va en forma base: Did she delete.
deletes: después de did el verbo va en forma base, sin -s: Did she delete.

items.q: She ___ the report before the meeting started.
items.e: 'before' + 2 eventos → el anterior en Past Perfect.

has finished: la frase está en pasado (before the meeting started): had finished.
was finishing: was finishing sería en progreso; before the meeting started indica que ya estaba terminado: had finished.
finish: falta el auxiliar; acción anterior: had finished (had + participio).

items.q: ___ you working when the alert went off?
items.e: Past Continuous: were + you + -ing.

Did: did va con verbo base; con working se usa were (Were you working).
Had: had va con participio; con working se usa were (Were you working).

items.e: they → were / weren't.

didn't be: el verbo be no usa did/didn't; su negativo es weren't.
hadn't: hadn't necesita un participio (hadn't been); acá be en pasado simple: weren't.

title: ¿Cuál oración es correcta? (tus errores comunes de pasado)

items.e: Did + verbo base.

Did she went?: después de did el verbo va en forma base: Did she go?
Did she goes?: después de did el verbo va en forma base, sin -s: Did she go?

items.e: didn't + base.

después de didn't el verbo va en forma base: didn't work.
el negativo del pasado simple se arma con didn't + verbo base.

o: He didn't went to the office.
He didn't go to the office.
He no went to the office.
items.a: He didn't go to the office.
items.e: didn't + base (go).

después de didn't el verbo va en forma base: didn't go.
en inglés el negativo es didn't + verbo base (no no).

items.e: hadn't + participio (gone), no went.

el participio de go es gone (go → went → gone): hadn't gone.
después de didn't el verbo va en forma base (didn't go); aquí además se pide past perfect: hadn't gone.

items.e: they → were.

Did they working?: did va con verbo base; con working se usa were: Were they working?

o: By the time I arrived, she finished the report.
By the time I arrived, she had finished the report.
By the time I arrived, she has finished the report.
items.a: By the time I arrived, she had finished the report.
items.e: 'By the time' → Past Perfect para la acción anterior.

By the time I arrived, she finished the: by the time marca que terminar fue ANTES de llegar: had finished.
By the time I arrived, she has finished: Present Perfect habla del presente; la frase está en pasado: had finished.

items.e: know es state verb: sin continuo.

know es un state verb y no se usa en forma continua: knew.
have + participio (known); además la frase está en pasado simple: knew.

o: I had ate before you arrived.
I had eaten before you arrived.
I had eat before you arrived.
items.a: I had eaten before you arrived.
items.e: eat → ate → eaten.

el participio de eat es eaten (eat → ate → eaten): had eaten.
había que usar el participio: eaten (eat → ate → eaten).

o: The server crashed because someone has deleted the wrong file.
The server crashed because someone had deleted the wrong file.
The server crashed because someone had delete the wrong file.
items.a: The server crashed because someone had deleted the wrong file.
items.e: La causa ocurrió antes del crash: had + participio.

The server crashed because someone has d: Present Perfect habla del presente; la historia está en pasado (crashed): had deleted.
